title: Annotatio IV §.VII close: Cyprian — invade the Lord’s body only spiritually; stop before §.VIII
pass_a_gloss: The third finally, and already having entered this age more deeply, holy CYPRIAN, most expressly of all sets forth that true and spiritual presence and participation of Christ’s body in the Eucharist — meanwhile in a rhetorical style (begun to be cultivated by the Fathers especially at this time, yet easily drawn into abuse, as in the popular sermon On the Lapsed, wont to indulge Rhetoric for itself and its nature) — among other things in this manner, while he inveighs against those who, having once denied the Christian faith, shortly after touched by milder penitence and so less prepared, approach the Sacred supper: Still almost belching, he says, the death-dealing foods of idols, with jaws still exhaling their crime and smelling of deadly contagions, they invade the Lord’s Body. And again. All these things despised and contemned, violence is done to the Body of Christ and His blood; now they offend more against the Lord with hands and mouth than when they denied the Lord. Hence indeed they could not invade Christ’s body, and do violence to it and His Blood, otherwise than in a Spiritual mode, namely taking Bread and Wine, or the Sacrament of the Lord, which the impious are not to usurp and handle except through Sacrilege.
pass_b_english: Cyprian, later in the century, most expressly teaches true spiritual presence and participation — in rhetorical style (On the Lapsed) against the unprepared who still reek of idol foods yet invade the Lord’s Body.
They can invade Christ’s body and do violence to His blood only in a Spiritual mode — by taking bread and wine, which the impious handle only by sacrilege.
source_text: Tertius denique & jam altius seculum hoc ingressus, divus CYPRIANUS, veram illam ac spiritualem corporis Christi in Eucharistia præsentiam atque participationem, disertissimè omnium, rhetoricô interim stylô (hôc potissimum tempore à Patribus excoli cœptô, facilè autem in abusum trahendo, in sermone de Lapsis populari, Rhetoricæ per se suamque naturam, indulgere solito) inter alia hunc in modum edisserit, dum nempe in eos invehitur, qui ab negatâ semel fide christiana, paulò post leniori pænitentiâ tacti, sicque minus præparati, ad S. cœnam accedunt: Mortiferos, ait, idolorum cibos adhuc penè ructantes, exhalantibus etiamnum scelus suum faucibus & contagia funesta redolentibus, Domini Corpus invadunt. Et iterum. Spretis his omnibus atque contemtis, vis infertur Corpori Christi & sanguini ejus; plus modò in Dominum manibus atque ore delinquunt, quàm cùm Dominum negaverunt. Hinc namque corpus Christi invadere, & huic, nec non Sanguini ejus, vim inferre aliter, quàm Spirituali modô, haud poterant, sumentes nempe Panem & Vinum, seu Sacramentum Domini, ab impiis non nisi per Sacrilegium, usurpandum & attrectandum.
